Our goal is to turn creative ideas into practical and interactive projects while learning and collaborating together. We welcome curious and dedicated participants who enjoy problem-solving and teamwork. We are especially looking for members with skills in programming, web development, UI/UX design, scientific research, and creative thinking.
summary:
EarthSound – Listen to Our Planet 🌍

EarthSound is a project designed to help people connect with our planet in a new and interesting way: by listening to it. Today, we can easily see environmental changes through graphs, maps, and satellite images, but not everyone finds it easy to understand this information. EarthSound aims to change that by turning environmental data into sounds that anyone can explore.

The application focuses on three important environmental indicators: temperature, rainfall, and vegetation. Each one produces different sounds depending on its values. For example, higher temperatures create higher-pitched sounds, rainfall changes the rhythm and intensity, while vegetation affects the sound's texture.

Users can explore interactive charts, listen to the generated sounds, and control the audio themselves. The project also introduces how NASA satellites observe Earth and collect valuable environmental information.

Inspired by NASA's Earth Information Jukebox challenge, EarthSound combines science, technology, and creativity to make environmental data more engaging and easier to understand.

Our goal is simple: help people not only see how our planet is changing, but actually hear it.
details:
EarthSound – Listen to Our Planet 🌍
EarthSound is an interactive web application that gives people a new way to understand our planet by turning environmental data into sound. Instead of only looking at numbers and graphs, users can actually listen to changes in the environment.
The application focuses on three environmental indicators: temperature, rainfall, and vegetation. Each indicator is translated into different sound characteristics using the Web Audio API. For example, higher temperatures produce higher-pitched sounds, rainfall controls the rhythm and intensity, and vegetation changes the sound's texture and frequency. Users can explore sample datasets, interact with animated charts, and play, pause, or adjust the volume of the generated sounds.
One of the main benefits of EarthSound is that it makes environmental information more accessible, engaging, and easier to understand. It offers an alternative way to explore scientific data, especially for people who may find traditional charts difficult to interpret. It can also encourage curiosity about climate change and the importance of protecting our planet.
Our intended impact is to help people develop a stronger connection with Earth's environment. By transforming scientific information into an auditory experience, we hope to make environmental changes more noticeable and encourage people to pay greater attention to the world around them.
We developed the project using React, Vite, and CSS for the interface and overall design. JavaScript handles the application logic, while the Web Audio API generates sounds directly in the browser. We also use interactive charts and CSS animations to create a more immersive experience. The application does not require paid APIs, subscriptions, or a backend. It uses sample demonstration datasets rather than presenting simulated values as real NASA observations.
What makes EarthSound creative is its approach to data visualization. We decided to go beyond simply showing environmental information and explore how it could be experienced through another human sense: hearing. We wanted to combine science, technology, music, and creativity in one accessible platform.
During development, we considered accessibility, simplicity, responsiveness, performance, and scientific accuracy. We also made sure to clearly distinguish demonstration data from actual NASA observations.
Ultimately, EarthSound is built around one simple idea: **What if we could hear our planet changing instead of only watching it happen?**
